55412.x: Photographing faint objects in the night sky takes long exposures, and the sky keeps moving while the shutter is open. Keeping a camera locked on a target usually takes a lot of setup.
Tinyphoton (Wuhan) Technology Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Imaging at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Draco.

Draco is a portable alt-azimuth system for long-exposure deep-sky imaging. Its 388mm-long, approximately 5.5kg body integrates a 90mm f/3.8 optical system, built-in autoguiding, physical field de-rotation, thermal control, dark-frame calibration and onboard image processing.

During an exposure, the guider measures stellar drift and sends corrections to the tracking system. The main imaging module rotates around the optical axis to counter field rotation produced by alt-azimuth tracking. These functions enable repeatable single-frame exposures up to 300 seconds without polar alignment or an external equatorial mount, wedge or guide scope.

The DWARFLAB app provides target selection, image acquisition, calibration, stacking and processing on a phone or tablet. Its open software layer and built-in coding agent support user-written scripts. PhotonLink allows remote access to a Draco installed at another location, while multiple units can contribute independently captured data to images with longer total integration or wider coverage.

55419.x: Visual inspection on a factory line requires imaging conditions and inspection criteria matched to each product's shape, material and surface characteristics. Conventional inspection systems are often built for specific products, so equipment and inspection criteria must be adjusted whenever production changes.

A.I.Matics, an AI image recognition company led by CEO Hoon Lee, took a software-based approach to the problem with AIM-T1, an AI vision inspection platform. The company recently announced that AIM-T1 won CES 2027 Innovation Awards in two categories: Artificial Intelligence and Construction & Industrial Tech.

The CES Innovation Awards are presented by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA) ahead of CES, the world's largest IT and consumer electronics show, based on an overall evaluation of technology, design and innovation. CES 2027 is scheduled for January 2027 in Las Vegas.

AIM-T1 combines modular hardware with inspection software. When production shifts to a different product, inspection criteria can be updated through software. The platform is designed to generate inspection models for new products using defect-free reference samples. The system combines in-context learning, which enables adaptation using reference examples, with world model technology.

On the hardware side, the optical unit uses a liquid lens and electronic focus stacking. Precise electronic focus control maintains image sharpness across products with different heights and surface characteristics. Field workers can set inspection conditions, check results and improve models through the dedicated software.

A.I.Matics began as an in-house venture at Hyundai Motor Company in 2000 and has since developed expertise in vehicle image recognition technology. Its proprietary AI engine, aimNet, runs in more than 520,000 vehicles. The company adapted that technology, made lightweight for vehicle environments, for manufacturing inspection equipment and unveiled AIM-T1 in April.

"Introducing a new product on a manufacturing line requires considerable time and expense to reconfigure inspection equipment and criteria," Lee said. "AIM-T1 shifts inspection from hardware-dependent systems to software-driven processes, allowing a single machine to handle a wider range of products." He added, "We will use this award to speed up our expansion into overseas markets, including North America."
A.I.Matics plans to present AIM-T1 at CES 2027 and meet manufacturers, automation equipment companies and distribution partners.

55425.x: QUAZAR Co., Ltd. (CEO Myunghyun Kim), a South Korean vision artificial intelligence enterprise, will exhibit at the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026, held from November 18 to 20 at Singapore EXPO. The company will showcase its proprietary platform, “QUAZAR Tagless DPP,” recognized as a CES 2027 Innovation Awards Honoree in the Enterprise Tech category. Built to address the European Union’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), the platform delivers end-to-end authentication and lifecycle tracking for consumer goods without requiring physical QR codes, RFID, or NFC tags.

Founded in June 2020 and headquartered in Bupyeong, Incheon, QUAZAR develops advanced computer vision technologies that identify microscopic product characteristics from standard photographic images. Expanding beyond industrial vision, the company has commercialized solutions spanning luxury goods authentication, digital product passports, and AI-driven bird deterrence systems. In 2025, QUAZAR recorded KRW 824 million in revenue and has secured KRW 600 million in cumulative Seed and Pre-A venture funding. Its R&D growth has been backed by national technology initiatives, including South Korea’s TIPS R&D program in 2024, the government startup commercialization program in 2025, Incheon Airport’s startup acceleration project in 2026, and designation as a Global IP Star Company. The enterprise holds four registered patents, has five pending applications, and is an active member of the Korea Intellectual Property Protection Agency’s anti-counterfeiting technology council.

The core highlight presented at SFF 2026, QUAZAR Tagless DPP, introduces a non-invasive identity-capture method that recognizes products directly by their intrinsic physical attributes. The system extracts a unique visual signature from natural manufacturing traces, such as stitching patterns, tooling impressions, and leather or textile grains. Authenticity is validated through a three-stage cross-verification engine combining a vision-language model (VLM), CLIP-Hash visual fingerprint matching, and an algorithmic decision layer modeled on expert appraisal methodologies. An integrated Explainable AI (XAI) module provides transparent rationales for each decision and, in the event of cross-model discrepancies, is backed by human specialist intervention. The platform’s authentication precision ranged from 94.5% to 95.7% in testing certified by the Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (KOLAS).

Verified product records are minted directly on the Polygon Layer-2 blockchain as non-transferable Soulbound Tokens (SBTs), with the underlying evidence securely distributed across the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) to ensure permanent, decentralized data availability. Over a product’s full lifecycle, subsequent events—such as secondary resale, professional repairs, and end-of-life recycling—are appended as linked tokens to the original passport. This architecture enables luxury, fashion, and footwear brands to comply seamlessly with EU ESPR take-back mandates and circularity disclosures via standard APIs and an enterprise console, eliminating the need to construct bespoke IT infrastructure.

55435.x: The steady roar that fills an aircraft cabin pours in partly through the windows, and headphones only block it at the ear. Stopping the noise at the glass itself reaches everyone on board.
AGC Inc. received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Travel & Tourism at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Glass Noise Cancellation (GNC) Module.

AGC's Glass Noise Cancellation (GNC) Module is an aircraft cabin window module that actively reduces noise transmitted through glass. A microphone or sensor detects exterior noise, and an actuator integrated with the glass generates opposite-phase vibrations to reduce sound entering the cabin, achieving noise reduction of up to about 10 dB in demo measurements on a mock-up.

Unlike headphone-based noise cancellation, GNC reduces noise at its transmission path without requiring passengers to wear personal devices, combining AGC's glass engineering and vibration-control expertise to turn glass into an active acoustic component while maintaining visibility and appearance.
Beyond aircraft, AGC envisions extending the technology to other mobility applications, including trains and automobiles, as well as architectural settings such as hotels.

55436.x: Training a robot by trial and error in the real world is slow, costly and hard on the hardware. Letting it practice inside a model of the world instead takes much of that burden off the physical machine.
Agibot was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Genie Envisioner 2.0, an embodied world model system.

Genie Envisioner 2.0 (GE 2.0) is an embodied world model system for robot training and evaluation, comprising the GE-Act world action model and the GE-Sim 2.0 world simulator. Given robot actions, it generates multi-view predictions of future scenes while simultaneously forecasting joint angles and gripper states.

Its built-in World Judge evaluates task outcomes against natural-language instructions and generates reward signals, so robot policies can be evaluated, refined through reinforcement learning and iteratively improved within model-generated environments.
This reduces reliance on physical robots and real-world experimental setups.

The battery is available for integration into wearables, asset trackers, smart gadgets and IoT devices.

55438.x: Tinnitus is a ringing in the ears with no outside source, and much of its burden is how much attention it commands. Learning to be less bothered by the sound is often the realistic goal.
Freequency bv. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Freequency, a smartphone app for people with tinnitus.
Freequency is a smartphone app built to help people with tinnitus become less bothered by it over time, based on two therapeutic principles: exposure therapy and mirror therapy.

Users first match the sound in the app to their own tinnitus. The app then uses augmented reality to represent the sound as a bird inside a cage, placed in the user's own surroundings and viewed through the phone's camera; the user searches for the bird and releases it from its cage, which temporarily stops the sound, after which a new bird appears and the exercise repeats.
By confronting users with their own tinnitus sound through a simple, interactive exercise, Freequency aims to help them feel more comfortable with and more in control of their tinnitus.

55439.x: Most sleep gadgets either just track the night or play the same fixed soundscape regardless of how the night actually goes. Reading the room and the sleeper, then adjusting through the night, is a harder loop to close.
Fullive AI Limited was named a 2027 Honoree in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Fullive Somni, a contactless bedside sleep system.

Fullive Somni is a contactless bedside sleep system that uses millimeter-wave and environmental sensing to understand personal sleep patterns and room conditions without a wearable. Its AI continuously refines an individualized sleep model and coordinates sound, light and scent in response to changing sleep states and environmental conditions throughout the night.

Rather than simply tracking sleep or delivering fixed sensory experiences, it creates a closed loop between sensing, personalized interpretation and adaptive multisensory support, and is designed to extend to connected bedroom devices, including temperature control, for broader environmental adaptation over time.

By operating quietly in the background it reduces the need for screens, wearables or repeated interaction, bringing sensing, adaptive intelligence and environmental support together in a single sculptural bedside object.

Glide is billed as the world's first "intelligent guide," an affordable personal mobility device for people who are blind, have low vision or are experiencing vision loss with age. Built on AI developed from the ground up for navigating unstructured pedestrian environments, it offers the blind and low-vision community a third option alongside the white cane and the guide dog.

With two all-terrain wheels and an adjustable telescoping handle, the user nudges Glide forward and lets it steer, as it physically guides them through familiar and new environments, avoiding obstacles and hazards, describing surroundings and identifying key information along the way.
Quick to learn and intuitive to use, whether for a trip to the local store or a busy airport, Glide is meant to give users the freedom to move independently and confidently on their own terms.

55442.x: Adding a screen to a product has always meant hauling in a driver chip, a controller, firmware and a battery sized for it. Shrinking all that down to something as simple as wiring up an LED opens displays to places they never fit before.
Luchrome was named a 2027 Honoree in Embedded Technologies at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Lunity.

Lunity sets out to turn the display into a simple component rather than a costly subsystem. For 50 years, adding a display meant adding a driver chip, a controller, firmware and a battery built around the screen; Lunity aims to make adding one as simple as connecting an LED, so a product gains the ability to communicate visually without carrying a full display subsystem.
It frames the problem as billions of connected objects still being unable to show the information they already have.

Lunity offers an energy-efficient display simple enough to run straight off any microcontroller, extending visual communication to wearables, packaging, labels and sensors where it was previously impossible.

55448.x: Fitness trackers are good at counting, less good at knowing when a hard day should become an easy one. Pushing a body without reading its limits is how training turns into injury.
Mosscode Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the MossCode PHI Modular Sports Watch.

MossCode PHI is a digital-health wearable that uses training and recovery as the pathway to health, tracking biometrics around the clock and turning those signals into guidance that respects the user's personal baseline.

A screenless Band with an optical sensor stays on the wrist and records heart rate at up to 100 Hz, along with heart-rate variability, sleep, stress and recovery status. A detachable display, the Dial, clicks onto the Band to form a GPS sports watch and recharges the Band while it stays on the wrist, so biomarker tracking never stops.

The MossCode App's AI coach places body biometrics and training data on one platform and sets each day's training target to the user's own baseline, building fitness while limiting the risk of overreaching.

55449.x: A horse cannot say when something feels wrong, and much of what matters to its health shows only in motion, out in the field or on the move. Catching the early signs usually means a trip to the clinic.
Myant received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Pet & Animal Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SKIIN Equine, a smart textile platform for equine care.

Worn as a comfortable girth band, SKIIN Equine captures cardiac, respiratory, temperature, biomechanical and behavioral data during normal activity, training, travel and competition, bringing continuous, clinically meaningful physiological monitoring into everyday care.

The system connects owners, trainers and veterinarians through consumer and clinical software, which the description says enables remote assessment, longitudinal tracking and faster identification of potential health risks.
By making advanced monitoring practical outside the clinic, the description says it supports earlier intervention, safer performance decisions and more proactive management of equine health.

55457.x: A breast ultrasound normally depends on a trained hand holding the probe, which keeps the exam inside the clinic. Catching something early is only possible if the screening actually happens.
NEOFORM and Hanseo University were named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for ONU, a clinician-connected home breast-screening system with guided ultrasound.

ONU judges ultrasound scan quality while the scan is still happening, the description says, so a lay user at home can produce clinician-reviewable breast images without operator training. It notes that five-year relative survival falls from 100 percent for localized breast cancer to 33.8 percent once disease is distant, yet routine screening is easy to postpone.

A circular smart-mirror display, a wireless linear-array probe and a charging dock guide preparation, probe positioning, scan direction and progress through visual and voice prompts, while ultrasound, motion, contact and position data are synchronized to evaluate handling stability, image quality and scan coverage during use. When incomplete areas are identified, the mirror guides location-specific rescanning before the session ends.

Powder-room placement links gel application to cleanup, and a modular architecture supports component-level replacement; the description says ONU extends breast-health management from isolated clinical visits to repeatable home participation while preserving mammography, professional interpretation and diagnosis.

NEXA was named a 2027 Honoree in Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for MegaConnect, a rugged portable 5G hotspot.

Powered by FirstNet MegaRange and 5G+, MegaConnect is a rugged, portable 5G HPUE hotspot for enterprise and public-sector use. With 1.25W transmission power, the highest allowed in the U.S., it delivers stronger signal reach and up to twice the upload throughput of standard devices in challenging environments.

The device supports up to 64 Wi-Fi connections and runs with no battery for continuous use, and built with Qualcomm Snapdragon and certified for FirstNet Trusted, it meets high security standards for mission-critical communications.

Designed in partnership with AT&T and FirstNet and leveraging AT&T and FirstNet MegaRange technology, MegaConnect provides extended coverage and improved reliability over traditional hotspots, with a compact form factor significantly smaller than other HPUE solutions for mobile teams in remote or high-demand conditions.

55459.x: Taking the mechanical column out of the steering wheel frees the cockpit to be arranged in new ways, but the wheel still has to feel connected to the road. Recreating that feedback electronically is the engineering test.
Nexteer Automotive was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the High Mount Direct Drive Steer-by-Wire Handwheel Actuator (HMDD).

Nexteer's High Mount Direct Drive Handwheel Actuator (HMDD) is a steer-by-wire component that captures driver steering inputs and converts them into electronic commands for the roadwheels, delivering road-feedback torque through a direct-drive motor and advanced control software.

Its stationary-hub design keeps the center section fixed relative to the driver, enabling consistent positioning of the airbag, controls and future center-hub features, while the compact, high-mount packaging supports alternative cockpit architectures and greater interior design flexibility.

HMDD incorporates fault-tolerant controls, dual-path communications and software-defined steering calibration that can be updated throughout the vehicle lifecycle, and it is designed for integration across internal-combustion, hybrid and electric platforms, supporting 12V and 48V architectures and left- and right-hand-drive configurations.

55460.x: A fitness ring or a tiny sensor has to think for itself, stay connected and run for days on a sliver of a battery, all at once. Fitting that into a single low-power chip is the constraint.
Nordic Semiconductor was named a 2027 Honoree in Embedded Technologies at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the nRF54LM20B wireless System-on-Chip.

The nRF54LM20B is an ultra-low-power wireless System-on-Chip for battery-powered connected products that need secure connectivity and on-device intelligence, the description says. It combines a 128 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 application processor, a 128 MHz RISC-V coprocessor, Nordic's proprietary 128 MHz Axon Neural Processing Unit, 2 MB non-volatile memory, 512 KB RAM, embedded security, peripherals and a multiprotocol 2.4 GHz radio in one device.

The integrated architecture supports TensorFlow Lite inference on the NPU and compact Neuton models on the CPU at the same time, plus wireless operation across Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Channel Sounding, Bluetooth Mesh, Matter, Thread, Zigbee, Aliro and proprietary 2.4 GHz protocols.

The description says it suits earbuds, fitness bands and rings, voice-controlled remotes and speakers, smart-home sensors, medical and industrial sensors, and asset trackers, where local inference improves responsiveness, privacy, battery life and product size.

55461.x: Nuvell Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Food Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for NUVELL Plantein, an automated plant-protein appliance.

NUVELL Plantein is an AI-powered smart countertop platform that fully automates plant-protein production, the description says. It consolidates high-speed blending, thermal processing, filtration, liquid transfer, coagulation and mechanical pressing into a single hands-free workflow.

Its integrated electromechanical architecture combines sensor-driven control, Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) thermal compensation and mechanized pressing to turn raw ingredients directly into fresh plant milk or pressed tofu, removing manual straining and hot-liquid transfers.

A companion app supports remote control, recipe management and personalized nutrition tracking, while an auto-cleaning cycle simplifies maintenance; the description frames it as turning a fragmented, multi-stage process into one connected appliance.
Making plant milk or tofu at home means blending, boiling, straining and pressing, with hot liquid moved from pot to pot. The mess and the hot transfers are what keep most people from bothering.
